narrative:
The machine learning model predicted a very high probability of failure—99.2%—for your bar exam attempt, which significantly influenced the decision to deny your law school application. This means that, based on the data and patterns observed in previous students, the model strongly suggests that you are likely to struggle with passing the exam on your first try.

The most influential factors in this prediction were your academic performance in your first and third years of school, as well as your family income. Your grades placed you in the lowest decile compared to accepted students, who typically performed much better. This indicates that your academic background may not have prepared you adequately for the challenges of the bar exam. 

Additionally, your LSAT score was notably below the average of accepted students, which further contributed to the model's assessment of your readiness. While your family income is in the upper-middle bracket, which is common among many successful applicants, it did not offset the concerns raised by your academic performance.

To improve your chances for future applications, consider focusing on enhancing your academic skills, perhaps through additional coursework or tutoring, and retaking the LSAT to achieve a higher score. Strengthening these areas could significantly alter your profile and increase your likelihood of success in law school and on the bar exam.
